data.hypothesis: A 32-thread block may improve scheduling for the all-pairs traversal by increasing the number of CTAs versus the 64- and 128-thread candidates. More CTAs may also add scheduling overhead, so the net effect must be measured rather than assumed.
data.notes: Only launch geometry changes; the kernel, force equations, traversal, memory strategy, and JSON key set remain unchanged. The baseline, 128-thread parent, and prior 64-thread candidate were reported correct across 11 cases. Their measured means were 0.0018526411 s, 0.0018288109 s, and 0.0018118426 s, respectively; these do not establish how 32 threads will perform. The controller should validate every supported size before comparing official timings.
transformations: Set block and items_per_block to 32 while keeping shared_memory_bytes at zero.
Left src/nbody_kernel.cu and its traversal, force equations, and memory strategy unchanged.
